reason: E1 shows coherent TiC nanoprecipitates enhance strength and ductility at ambient and 800 °C via dislocation transmission, but does not test above 1000 °C or measure toughness. E2 shows TiC dispersion improves heat flux resistance, creep strength, and recrystallization temperature, but does not address coherent interfaces, dislocation bridging, or toughness. The key premises about high-temperature (>1000 °C) plastic strain and toughness enhancement by coherent TiC are not directly supported by the cited evidence.
premises: Coherent TiC nanoprecipitates facilitate dislocation transmission and relieve stress concentrations
TiC dispersion increases high-temperature strength, creep resistance, and recrystallization temperature
TiC at grain boundaries provides grain boundary strengthening and resists migration at elevated temperatures
The mechanism of dislocation bridging by coherent precipitates delays crack initiation and enhances ductility/toughness
The proposed mechanism operates above ~1000 °C in BCC refractory alloys
